questions.title: When Your Ball Hits Another Ball on the Green
questions.question: You putt your ball from the green, and it accidentally rolls into another ball that was already on the green and not moving. What should you do?

choices.text: You get 2 extra shots added. Play your ball from where it stopped and put the other ball back where it was.
You have to take your putt again with no extra shots.
You keep playing as normal with no extra shots.
Both balls stay where they finished and you play from there.

questions.explanation: If you putt on the green and hit another ball that was already sitting there, you get 2 penalty shots. Play your ball from where it rolled, and put the other ball back where it was before.

vocabulary.simpleMeaning: A soft hit with your club to make the ball roll on the green towards the hole.
Extra shots that get added to your score when you break a rule.
Play the ball from where it ended up after the shot.

questions.teachingTip: Let young golfers know it is important to watch for other balls on the green before they putt.
likelyMisconceptions: Children may think there is no penalty when balls hit each other on the green.
They may think they have to play from the new spots without moving any balls.

questions.title: Ball striking another ball on the green
questions.question: In stroke play, you putt from the green and your ball accidentally hits another ball at rest on the green. What do the rules say?

choices.text: You get 2 penalty strokes. Play your ball as it lies and replace the moved ball.
You must replay your shot with no penalty.
You continue play with no penalty.
Both balls are played from where they finished.

questions.explanation: In stroke play, if your ball played from the putting green hits another at rest on the green, you get two penalty strokes. You play your ball as it lies and replace the other ball.
